Normalise the remote_ratio column

Source: R/normalisation.R
normalize_remote_ratio.Rd

Clean and standardise the remote_ratio column of a data.frame. Ensures that values are numeric and between 0 and 100.

Usage

normalize_remote_ratio(data, binary = FALSE, threshold = 50)

Arguments

data

The data.frame containing the remote_ratio column.

binary

Logical (default FALSE). Activates binary mode (only 0 or 100).

threshold

Numeric (default 50). Threshold for binarisation.

  • If value >= threshold: becomes 100.

  • If value < threshold: becomes 0.

Value

The data.frame with the corrected remote_ratio column.

Details

The processing includes:

  • Conversion to numeric (conversion errors become NA).

  • Bounding values (pmin/pmax): anything < 0 becomes 0, anything > 100 becomes 100.

  • (Optional) Binarisation: If binary = TRUE, values become either 0 or 100 according to the threshold.

See also

Other Normalization functions: normalize_all(), normalize_factor()

Examples

df <- data.frame(remote_ratio = c("0", "100", "50", "30", "-5", "abc"))

# Standard normalisation (numeric + bounding 0-100)
normalize_remote_ratio(df)
#>   remote_ratio
#> 1            0
#> 2          100
#> 3           50
#> 4           30
#> 5            0
#> 6           NA

# Binary normalisation (everything >= 50 becomes 100, the rest 0)
normalize_remote_ratio(df, binary = TRUE, threshold = 50)
#>   remote_ratio
#> 1            0
#> 2          100
#> 3          100
#> 4            0
#> 5            0
#> 6           NA
